question: Should `axorc` become a supported standalone Homebrew-installed CLI, and if so should the formula consume release binaries or build tagged source?
rationale: The repository exposes and documents the CLI, but neither current release infrastructure nor project policy establishes a supported standalone distribution contract; choosing that contract affects ongoing releases and coordination with Peekaboo.

options.title: Ship release binaries
options.body: Publish a versioned universal or per-architecture macOS archive and install it through the official OpenClaw tap, matching the established Peekaboo distribution pattern.

options.title: Build from source
options.body: Add a source formula that builds the tagged Swift package, accepting a Swift toolchain dependency and slower installation in exchange for simpler release artifacts.

options.title: Keep CLI developer-only
options.body: Decline standalone AXorcist packaging and clarify that end users should use the supported Peekaboo CLI while `axorc` remains a source-build tool.

recommendation.title: Ship release binaries
recommendation.body: Publish a versioned universal or per-architecture macOS archive and install it through the official OpenClaw tap, matching the established Peekaboo distribution pattern.

likelyOwner.reason: The release history and signed tags make `steipete` the strongest available owner for the standalone distribution and tap contract.
